output.summary: KEP-2395 proposes removing in-tree cloud provider code from k8s.io/kubernetes in four phases, moving provider code to staging, building external cloud-controller-managers, freezing legacy code, and finally disabling in-tree providers by default. Its status is implemented at stage stable.
output.rationale: The project wants cloud providers to develop and release independently of the core Kubernetes cycle. Core components would also stop depending on cloud-specific APIs, which yields smaller binaries and fewer external-dependency security risks. The readme states the goal as removing all cloud provider specific code from k8s.io/kubernetes with minimal disruption.

alternatives.option: Remove in-tree providers in a single step
alternatives.why_not: The readme's stated goal is removal 'with minimal disruption to end users and developers', so it uses a phased approach instead; the sources do not discuss a single-step alternative further.

evidence.quote: Remove all cloud provider specific code from the `k8s.io/kubernetes` repository with minimal disruption to end users and developers.
Each cloud provider is free to release features/bug fixes at their own schedule rather than relying on the core Kubernetes release cycle.
A 4 phase approach will be taken. 1. Move all code in `k8s.io/kubernetes/pkg/cloudprovider/providers/<provider>` to `k8s.io/kubernetes/staging/src/k8s.io/legacy-cloud-providers/<provider>/`.
Disable in-tree providers and set the `DisableCloudProviders` and `DisableKubeletCloudCredentialProvider` feature gates to true by default.
It will necessarily require an increased level of turbulence for developers and users as they learn about the changes to the `kubelet`, `kube-apiserver`, and `kube-controller-manager` processes
